title: Resistance: Defining the Enemy
coreMove: Name the specific face Resistance is wearing for you today in one short phrase before you try to push through it.

exampleSpecs.domain: a forty-one-year-old paramedic finishing a night shift who has been almost-writing a memoir about her father's last year for three years
exampleSpecs.audience: a reader who has been carrying an unfinished personal project past the point of comfort
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether she opens the document tonight or files another excuse that sounds like reason
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she catches Resistance speaking in her own voice, mid-sentence, and names it out loud in the parking lot before unlocking the car

exampleSpecs.domain: a luthier in a small shop deciding whether to start the difficult inlay on a commissioned guitar or first reorganize the bench for the fourth time this week
exampleSpecs.audience: a craftsperson who confuses preparation with avoidance
exampleSpecs.stakes: a delivery date that is no longer abstract and a customer who has already paid half
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the luthier identifies tidying as the day's costume Resistance is wearing and refuses to begin tidying until the inlay is started

exampleSpecs.domain: a high school chemistry teacher who has wanted to apply to a doctoral program for six years and keeps redesigning the personal statement instead of submitting
exampleSpecs.audience: a mid-career reader stalled at the edge of a bigger life
exampleSpecs.stakes: a hard application deadline twelve days out and the private knowledge that the statement was good enough in March
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the teacher writes the sentence "Resistance is rewriting today" on a sticky note and submits without another revision

exampleSpecs.domain: a defense attorney and her paralegal at 7:42 a.m. before a trial-prep block she has rescheduled four times
exampleSpecs.audience: a reader who outsources their own avoidance to other people's urgencies
exampleSpecs.stakes: a client's case and the attorney's standing with the bench
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the paralegal asks what is actually stopping her and the attorney answers in one phrase, not a paragraph

exampleSpecs.domain: a retired infantry sergeant trying to start a woodworking YouTube channel after thirty years of saying he would
exampleSpecs.audience: a reader who has wanted to make something public for a long time and has not
exampleSpecs.stakes: his sense of what the rest of his life is for
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he lists, in his own plain words, the four faces Resistance wore this week and recognizes the one wearing his late father's voice

exampleSpecs.domain: a single father of a seven-year-old trying to finish a screenplay during the ninety minutes between drop-off and his shift at the warehouse
exampleSpecs.audience: a reader with thin slivers of time and a real project inside those slivers
exampleSpecs.stakes: the ninety minutes today, not the screenplay in the abstract
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: before, he opens email first and loses the slot; after, he says the phrase "not today" to the inbox and opens the script cold
